# restate_cloud_environment (Resource)

A Restate Cloud environment.

Creation is asynchronous: the API acknowledges the request and provisions in the background, so the provider polls until the environment is `ACTIVE`. A failed provision leaves the environment in place and reports its ID, so it can be inspected or destroyed.

The connection metadata this resource exports -- notably `admin_base_url` -- cannot configure a provider in the same apply, because Terraform must configure a provider before any resource exists. See the two-stage bootstrap guide.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "restate_cloud_environment" "production" {
  name    = "production"
  region  = "us-east-1"
  tier_id = "BUSINESS"

  # Destroying an environment is irreversible and takes its data with it. Clearing this guard is a
  # separate, deliberate apply.
  deletion_protection = true

  # Provisioning is asynchronous. The provider polls until the environment is ACTIVE, so the
  # connection metadata below is populated by the time the apply finishes.
  timeouts {
    create = "30m"
    delete = "30m"
  }
}

# Pass this to your service deployments so they can verify that a request came from Restate.
output "signing_public_key" {
  value = restate_cloud_environment.production.signing_public_key
}

# Configures the Admin API provider of a *later* stage, never one in this apply.
output "admin_base_url" {
  value = restate_cloud_environment.production.admin_base_url
}

output "ingress_base_url" {
  value = restate_cloud_environment.production.ingress_base_url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Environment name. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 63 characters, not starting or ending with a hyphen. Renaming is applied in place.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) When true, `terraform destroy` refuses to delete this environment. Destroying an environment is irreversible and takes its data with it, so guard production environments with this and clear it deliberately when you mean to tear one down.
- `region` (String) Region to place the environment in, for example `us-east-1`. When omitted, Restate Cloud picks the account's default and the provider records it, so later plans converge.

Changing it replaces the environment: the API has no migration operation, so there is no way to move an environment between regions. Use `restate_cloud_regions` to see what the account may use.
- `tier_id` (String) Environment tier: one of `FREE`, `STARTER`, `BUSINESS`, `PREMIUM`. When omitted, Restate Cloud applies its default and the provider records it.

`CUSTOM` is readable but cannot be requested: a custom tier is selected through an operator-configured profile, which the API does not report, so a custom-tier environment could not be refreshed without hidden drift.

A tier change on a Stripe-billed account may require completing a browser payment flow, which Terraform cannot do. The apply fails with an actionable error rather than reporting success; check `restate_cloud_account.billing_mode` first.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) Account the environment belongs to. It is recorded so a later plan can detect a provider pointed at a different account, and it is the first half of the import ID.
- `admin_base_url` (String) Base URL of this environment's Admin API. Use it as the `admin_url` of a provider configured in a later stage; it cannot configure a provider in the same apply.
- `id` (String) Environment ID assigned by Restate Cloud, for example `env_1a2b3c`.
- `ingress_base_url` (String) Base URL for invoking services in this environment.
- `invocation_metrics_url` (String) URL for this environment's invocation metrics. Empty when the API reports none.
- `proxy_base_url` (String) Base URL of the proxy service for this environment.
- `region_display_name` (String) Human-readable region label. Empty when the API reports none.
- `signing_public_key` (String) Public key services use to verify that a request came from this environment. Pass it to your service deployments so they can authenticate Restate.
- `status` (String) Provisioning status: `PENDING`, `ACTIVE`, `FAILED`, or `DELETED`. A successful apply always leaves this `ACTIVE`; it is exported for diagnostics.
- `tunnel_base_url` (String) Base URL of the private tunnel service for this environment.
- `tunnel_srv` (String) SRV record the tunnel client resolves to reach this environment.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Environments are imported by account ID and environment ID together. The account is part of the
# identity so importing into a provider configured for a different account is refused rather than
# silently adopting an environment from elsewhere.
terraform import restate_cloud_environment.production acc_1a2b3c/env_1a2b3c
```
